title: Hybrid VPC bridge: multi-AZ on-prem reference & onboarding playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope

This draft playbook describes a reference architecture and tactical onboarding steps for customers who require a hybrid VPC bridge between Redwood Private control plane and customer on-prem / colo multi-AZ deployments. The goal is to give field engineering and SREs a compact, repeatable path for: connectivity, routing, secure service exposure, Terraform module adoption, and an upgrade/rollback plan for baseline network changes.

Audience
- Solutions engineers performing first-3 customer activations for hybrid patterns
- Private deployments eng team owners and SREs
- Customer network/infra architects working with Redwood implementation teams

High-level architecture summary
- Customer runs private tenant workloads in one or more on-prem regions (AZs) or colocations.
- Redwood Private control plane remains in a managed VPC (hosted or customer-managed in their cloud).
- We establish a resilient edge: two or more physical links (cross-connects / SD-WAN tunnels) from customer edge to Redwood ingress (transit VPC or regional gateway).
- Border routing via EBGP across the links; optional EVPN for layer-2 bridging where required by customer.
- Transit GW implements VRFs / route-isolation per tenant, and policy-enforced egress via NAT or proxy.
- Service endpoints in the customer VPC (or on-prem) are fronted by a secure ingress proxy that validates mutual TLS and enforces RBAC.

Constraints and assumptions
- Customer has serviceable WAN links for BGP or supports IPsec/IKEv2 tunnels.
- Customer is willing to accept route advertisements for a small delegated prefix (recommended) or use NAT-based peering if prefix delegation is not possible.
- MD5 or TTL security for BGP is optional; prefer mTLS and control-plane ACLs for stronger auth.

Design patterns and options (decision matrix)
1) Direct BGP over cross-connect (preferred when colocated)
   - Pros: low latency, predictable paths, full route transparency
   - Cons: requires coordination with colo and supports direct prefix advertisement
2) IPsec tunnels with BGP (recommended for on-prem over internet or SD-WAN)
   - Pros: secure, works across internet, supports route exchange
   - Cons: higher jitter; needs monitoring and rekey policies
3) mTLS-proxied API traffic (application-layer fallback)
   - Pros: easiest for customers who cannot open IPsec/BGP; no prefix changes needed
   - Cons: higher latency and does not expose arbitrary services

Onboarding checklist (quick win sequence)
- Pre-kickoff: collect ASN, public ASN (if customer has), CIDR ranges, colo PO/AP locations, NTP/clock policy, list of endpoints to expose.
- Week 0 (prep): exchange contact lists, define maintenance windows, create Jira onboarding ticket, create Terraform workspace in private repo (branch naming: onboarding/customer-shortname).
- Week 1 (connectivity): provision cross-connect or SD-WAN tunnel; verify physical link; BGP session lab test (peer IPs, ASN, timers).
- Week 2 (routing & security): push initial Terraform modules for route filters, prefix-lists, and security groups; validate inbound/outbound flows with allowed-ports smoke tests.
- Week 3 (service cutover): flip DNS to new endpoints, monitor traffic, enable health checks; fallback plan tested and on standby.
- Week 4 (stabilize & QA): run load tests, enable observability dashboards (RTT, loss, route flaps), finalize runbook and handover docs.

Terraform module notes (practical guidance)
- Module layout suggestion: modules/network (pv-bridge), modules/bgp, modules/tunnels, modules/dns, modules/monitoring.
- Keep BGP and tunnel resources idempotent and parameterized: peer_asn, local_asn, peer_ip, pre_shared_key, ike_version.
- Example (pseudo-snippet to copy into onboarding module - plain text):
  resource "redwood_vpc_bridge_bgp" "peer" {
    name = "${var.customer}-bgp-1"
    peer_asn = var.customer_asn
    local_asn = var.redwood_asn
    peer_ip = var.peer_ip
    local_ip = var.local_ip
    hold_time = var.hold_time
    auth_password = var.bgp_md5 // optional
  }

- Secrets management: never author PSKs in repo; use secret injection via SSM/Secrets Manager or customer KMS/HSM when requested.
- Versioning: add a module variable module_version and a CHANGELOG.md in modules root; annotate breaking changes and required migration steps.

Upgrade/rollout and rollback plan (network changes)
- Always run changes during a low-traffic maintenance window agreed with customer.
- Staged rollout for routing changes: test in staging VRF -> canary VRF -> all VRFs.
- Pre-upgrade steps: capture current BGP table, traceroute baselines, and tcpdump on edge for a 10-minute window.
- Upgrade steps: apply Terraform in plan-only mode, review plan with network engineer, apply to a single edge pair, validate reachability and route propagation for 15 minutes, then expand.
- If routes fail to propagate or reachability breaks: trigger terraform rollback via stored plan or manually revert to last-known-good module tag; re-establish previous BGP timers.

Operational runbook snippets
- BGP flaps: recommended debug flow: check BGP counters -> show ip bgp neighbors -> verify MTU mismatches -> check IKE SA if tunnels are used.
- Latency spike triage: compare ping to colo cross-connect vs internet path; check traffic shaping on SD-WAN; correlate with CPU/GPU load on serving nodes.
- Certificate rotation: use automation to rotate mTLS certs 30 days out; maintain a rolling overlap of at least 7 days.

Security and compliance notes
- Use RBAC for route acceptance; limit who can update route filters in Terraform.
- Encrypt sensitive flows via IPsec or mTLS; log all peer changes and store in immutable audit logs (S3 with object lock or customer-provided logging service).
- For regulated customers: offer on-prem HSM for key storage, and redact sensitive route details in shared runbooks.

Testing and QA checklist
- Connectivity: 5 min ping, 1 min traceroute, verify AS path lengths are expected.
- Functionality: run Redwood health-check against private endpoints, validate token auth and short-lived signing keys.
- Load test: simulate steady-state tokenized traffic (sample workload) to ensure KV cache warm-up and prefix hit-rates are within 10% of hosted baseline.
- Chaos test (optional): bring down one cross-connect for 10 minutes and validate graceful failover within target SLO.

Known risks and mitigations
- Risk: AS path leaks to customer internet. Mitigation: strict prefix filters and BGP community tagging, validate via route collectors.
- Risk: MTU mismatches across VLANs and tunnels. Mitigation: standardize on 1500/9000 and test with jumbo frame probes.
- Risk: Drift between Terraform state and actual colo provisioning. Mitigation: run nightly state reconciliation jobs and notify if drift detected.

Handover checklist to customer ops
- Provide final Terraform module tag and instructions to run plan and apply in read-only mode.
- Deliver a single-page operations playbook: contact list, maintenance window cadence, fallback commands, and how to trigger rollback.
- Schedule a 2-hour ops run-through session and record it for customer runbook library.

Appendix: useful commands and short examples
- BGP show example (vendor-neutral):
  show bgp neighbors <peer_ip>
  show route summary
  show ip route <prefix>

- Packet capture quick filter to validate GRE/IPsec: ip proto 50 or port 500 or udp port 4500

- Terraform quick-call: terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.out && terraform apply plan.out

Notes / open questions
- Confirm whether customer requires EVPN L2 bridging for legacy appliances (design currently treats EVPN as special-case).
- Decide on standard hold-time and keepalive values across all onboarding docs (proposal: keepalive 10s, hold 30s).
- Align on drift detection alerting frequency: immediate vs daily batch.

References and follow-ups
- LINK: Confluence design doc (CONFLUENCE-1234) for detailed EVPN appendix
- ACTION: follow up with colo contacts to document cross-connect provisioning SLA in onboarding checklist (owner: Ben Hsu)

Status and next steps
- This is a working draft intended for the next two onboarding pilots. Please comment inline in the Google Drive doc and add any missing vendor-specific commands (Cisco/Juniper/Arista) to the Appendix.

Document history

- Review updates 2024-12-10 (BGP auth notes)
- Added upgrade rollback section 2025-01-15
